articleTitle: MV overhead lines using XLPE covered conductors. Scandinavian experience and NORWEB developments
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Review of Options for Overhead Rural Distribution
abstract: After 15 years of experience with MV covered overhead line systems in Scandinavia, components, system and installation practices have reached a state of established technology. The system offers phase clearance of only 50 cm and the ability to allow grounded objects to touch the line and phases to touch each other, without any tripping or customer outage. A substantial improvement in service reliability and a reduction in life cycle costs, compared to bare lines, is achieved. The aluminium alloy conductor is covered with black UV-resistant XLPE and filled with grease, to provide corrosion protection and longitudinal watertightness. Arcing guides are applied at insulator tops, to protect the line from arcing damages. Methods for determining the necessary frequency of arcing guides have been developed, based on probabilistic approaches. NORWEB plc has adapted the Norwegian covered line concept, realizing it through test sites and by defining a NORWEB design for their further development in accordance with the UK Electricity Supply Regulations of 1988.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Review of Options for Overhead Rural Distribution
abstract: Low voltage aerial bundled conductor (ABC) lines were first installed on the rural Irish distribution networks in 1981. The type chosen was the fully self supporting design closely following type NFA2X according to the VDE specification 0274. ABC is now the standard LV line type installed in the Republic of Ireland with over 17000 km of line length in service. This is growing at a rate of 1500 km per year. 25% of the LV overhead network is now comprised of ABC. This paper deals briefly with the countrywide introduction programme of low voltage ABC, the design choices made, problems encountered, developments made and assesses the economic and technical performance to date. It also touches on HV ABC and sets out the Irish utility position on this developing technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Review of Options for Overhead Rural Distribution
abstract: This paper looks at some of the issues associated with the specification and application of reclosers and sectionalisers. To do this, three possible schemes are considered followed by some practical issues associated with the implementation of the schemes. The three schemes are the traditional scheme, the enhanced traditional scheme, and the optimum scheme. For each scheme the author discusses the operation of the reclosers and sectionalisers upon a distribution network fault. The remote control of these devices is also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The manufacturer/user relationship in the development of accessories and fittings for overhead lines
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Review of Options for Overhead Rural Distribution
abstract: Adoption of insulated overhead line conductor systems are symptomatic of the exposure to which UK users have become as to how other nations engineer their distribution networks. For UK manufacturers, servicing these new innovations with accessories becomes a real challenge for the following reasons: we have equipped our production units to efficiently and economically produce connectors for traditional open wire, bare conductor installations; for the insulated conductors, not only is the production tooling investment mostly inappropriate but also the R and D test equipment; and conversely, the manufacturer in the countries from which UK users are taking the new technology have for some years built up their production units and R and D facilities, for what is to them standard product. The author discusses wider issues involved and the use of standards.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Economic and environmental considerations. A review of past and present practices (distribution network planning)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Review of Options for Overhead Rural Distribution
abstract: The strategic planning of any distribution system cannot be divorced from the economic and environmental considerations. The relative importance and priority of each aspect has and will continue to be dependent upon the social and political factors of the day. Here, the author describes how the thrust of technological developments seem to be focused on: (i) making underground systems as cheap as overhead networks; or (ii) making overhead systems "operationally" like underground systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Japanese approach to overhead distribution-a ScottishPower view
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Review of Options for Overhead Rural Distribution
abstract: The Japanese distribution system is quite different to anything in the UK. It looks different, it is designed differently and it is operated differently but, most significantly, it offers the worlds best levels of service to its customers. This presentation offers a description of some of the main characteristics of Japanese operations, the motives behind them and the impressive performance levels achieved. The Kyushu Electric Power Company (Kepco) distribution network is used as the example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New technology in the management of distribution overhead line assets
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Review of Options for Overhead Rural Distribution
abstract: Whilst recognising the contribution that can be made by the introduction of new technologies into the design and building of overhead lines Eastern Group believes that a major contribution to the improvement in reliability, safety and reduction in operating cost can be made by improvements in the way an overhead line asset is managed. This presentation outlines the process which Eastern sees as being necessary and has begun to introduce to this important business sector.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Review of Options for Overhead Rural Distribution
abstract: This paper reviews the performance of present UK overhead power line overcurrent protective devices (expulsion fuses, liquid fuses and current-limiting fuses) and argues the case for their continued use in the majority of applications. The paper then goes on to highlight two more recently developed devices-the full-range fuse and the automatic sectionalising link-each capable of bringing a higher level of overall performance to existing power systems on a selective basis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
